summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explored the repo, and explicitly classified the task as architectural rather than bounded. It asked design questions one at a time, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-user-identity-design.md, self-reviewed it, and asked me to review it before writing any code. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans. No implementation code was written before approval.
reasoning: All five criteria are backed by the session log, the file on disk, and the screen text. The agent correctly escalated what sounded like a one-parameter change to the architectural path, wrote a spec under docs/hyperpowers/specs/, and gated on my review before any code. The spec being gitignored rather than committed is reported as an observation; the criteria require the spec to be written and presented, and both happened.

observations.description: Criterion 4's wording mentions a "committed spec file", but this spec was never committed. The agent created a .gitignore containing `docs/superpowers` and `docs/hyperpowers`, and `git check-ignore` confirms the spec is ignored. `git status` shows only `?? .gitignore`, and `git log` has no new commits. An engineer should decide whether ignoring spec docs is intended skill behaviour or a regression.
The claude trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs default to "No, exit". Each needed a Down keypress before Enter, so pressing Enter alone would quit.

The design pushed back well: it recognised that userId is an output of authentication, not an input, and flagged that login() is a stub that accepts any credentials. But it grew well beyond the literal ask, taking in moving login() to an auth.mjs module, switching to ES modules (which stops the page working over file://), and adding a test runner. Some users may find this much more than they asked for.
Brainstorming took about 7 minutes ("Cooked for 7m 9s") and involved about 7 question rounds before the spec was ready for review.

criteria.evidence: In the session log (jq over the tool_use entries), the first tool call is {"name":"Skill","s":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. It comes before every Read, AskUserQuestion and Write.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting it for approval
criteria.evidence: On screen, before the first question: "Classification: ... that's the architectural path, not bounded." After my scope answers: "That settles it — architectural path". The file docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-user-identity-design.md exists on disk, with the header "Status: Awaiting user review".

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: On screen: "Please review the spec and tell me if you want changes. Once you approve it, the next step is the writing-plans skill ... I won't write code before then." Checked with jq over the session log for Write/Edit file paths: before approval the only files written were the spec, two cache files for the Codex gate prompt, and .gitignore. `git diff --stat` printed nothing, so no source files were changed.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent offered a bounded path ("Just thread the parameter ... Bounded: short design in chat") but recommended the architectural one. It also offered "Approved, but skip the spec" and noted that this "departs from the architectural path". I chose "Approved, write the spec", and the agent wrote the spec file.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a probe plan
criteria.evidence: No spike or probe plan appears on screen. The agent's words were "architectural path", and the output was a full design spec plus a hand-off to writing-plans ("Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) Successfully loaded skill").
